crew_summary: 511 aircrew killed with 207 Squadron from RAF Spilsby, October 1943–October 1945; 104 with no known grave
narrative: 207 Squadron flew Lancasters from RAF Spilsby in Lincolnshire from October 1943. In just over two years of operations, 511 aircrew were killed — 104 of them with no known grave, their names commemorated on the Runnymede Memorial. The squadron drew crew from across the Commonwealth and Allied nations: Great Britain, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the United States, the Netherlands, and Eire. The church of All Saints at Great Steeping, the village nearest RAF Spilsby, was chosen to house the memorial plaque dedicated on VE Day anniversary, 8 May 1992. The church also contains a 44 Squadron memorial tablet — both squadrons shared RAF Spilsby from September 1944 to July 1945, making All Saints a dual point of remembrance for two of Bomber Command's Lancaster squadrons. The church is publicly accessible throughout the year.
memorial_details: Memorial plaque inside All Saints Church, Great Steeping. Records 511 aircrew killed with 207 Squadron from RAF Spilsby, October 1943 to October 1945, of whom 104 have no known grave. Also commemorates 12 ground staff. The church also contains a 44 Squadron memorial tablet — both squadrons shared RAF Spilsby Sep 1944–Jul 1945. IWM War Memorials Register reference: IWM 55134.
